Since postponement can sometimes stem from ignorance of the enemies' sins, He said, negating that: ﴿And indeed your Lord﴾, meaning: and the situation is that He indicated by the attribute of Lordship [His] postponing them, as a kindness to Him and an honouring of him. ﴿Knows﴾, meaning: with a knowledge unlike your knowledge, rather one that is in the utmost disclosure before Him, its subtle and its grand. ﴿what their breasts conceal﴾, meaning: what they harbour, hide and keep secret ﴿their breasts﴾, meaning: all of the people, let alone your people. ﴿and what they disclose﴾, meaning: what they manifest of their enmity towards you, so do not fear them. He mentioned this division because open declaration is more soothing to the soul, and the discourse calls for elaboration; moreover, in public declaration there may be clamour and a confusion of voices which becomes a cause of concealment.

The Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 27, verse 75:

Since the constancy of the reasons of people is, for the most part, restricted to the Book, He said, to bring it closer to their understanding: ﴿And there is not a hidden thing [i.e., a single hidden matter of the hidden matters] in the utmost concealment﴾ ﴿in the heaven and the earth﴾, that is, in whatever place of them it may be. He used the singular forms (heaven and earth) to indicate the intended sense of the genus, encompassing every individual. ﴿Except that it is in a Book﴾ which He wrote before bringing them into existence, because nothing comes to be except by His knowledge and His decree. ﴿Clear﴾, nothing in it is concealed from whoever knows it from Him, however it may be.

Then He indicated this by His saying: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an﴾, i.e., that which this unlettered Prophet has brought, who had not known any knowledge before it and had not mixed with any scholar, ﴿relates﴾, i.e., continues to report and recounts piece by piece, in a manner of certainty with no doubt in it, without addition or deficiency, ﴿to the Children of Israel﴾, i.e., whose reports are preserved in their books, and of which only a few of their most skilled scholars know some, ﴿most of that about which they﴾, i.e., in particular, because it is among their special reports of which no one other than them has knowledge, ﴿differ﴾, i.e., concerning matters of religion, even though they exerted themselves in concealing it, such as the story of the married adulterer, in that they concealed that its prescribed punishment is stoning, and the story of ʿUzayr and the Messiah, and the Prophet ﷺ's bringing out of that from their Torah. Thus it is established, by its verification through the tongue of one who had never acquired any knowledge, that it is from Allah. And it is established that Allah, exalted is He, knows everything, since there is no particularity in this with respect to His knowledge, glory be to Him, over anything else.

(p-212) When the proof of His knowledge became clear through this, He followed it with the proof of His grace and forbearance, saying: ﴿And indeed it﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿is surely a guidance﴾, that is, one that conveys to the intended goal for whoever is granted success, ﴿and a mercy﴾, that is, a blessing and an honour, ﴿for the believers﴾, that is, those whom it has imprinted with faith, so that it (faith) is an firmly established attribute of theirs, just as it is ﴿for the disbelievers, a deafness in their ears and a blindness in their hearts﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 27, verse 78:

When he had mentioned the proof of His grace, he followed it with the proof of His justice, saying, beginning anew in answer to one who might think that His grace is constantly general to both groups: ﴿Indeed﴾, and he said: ﴿your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who does good to you by gathering for each of them knowledge, eloquence, religion, excellence, worldly life, chastity and courage, as consolation to the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿will judge between them﴾, i.e., between all those left behind, ﴿by His judgment﴾, i.e., which is the most just, most perfect, most effective and most excellent judgment, despite their disbelief in Him and their mockery of His messengers, not by the judgment of other than Him, nor by a deputy He appoints. ﴿And He﴾, i.e., while the state is that He Himself is ﴿the Mighty﴾, so no command of His is turned back, ﴿the Knowing﴾, so no secret or open matter is hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 27, verse 79:

When knowledge and wisdom, and greatness and power, were established for him, there followed from this His saying: ﴿So put your trust in Allah﴾, that is, in the One who possesses all greatness, by virtue of the knowledge and power through which He established that you are the greatest of His chosen servants, in the face of the mockery of the enemies and whatever else comes from their confrontation with you and their peaceful dealings with you, so that you may leave all affairs to Him and rest from bearing hardships, trusting in His support. How excellent is the saying of Qays ibn al-Khatim, who was from the pre-Islamic era: (p-213)

؎ مَتى ما تَقُدْ بِالباطِلِ الحَقَّ يَأْبَهُ وإنْ تَقُدِ الأطْوارَ بِالحَقِّ تَنْقُدِ

Then He gave the reason for this, as an exhortation to diligence in deeds and as a restraint for the people of falsehood from wishing for the impossible, so He said: ﴿Indeed, you are upon the clear truth﴾, that is, clear in itself and making clear to others. Your right does not perish, and its clarity is not hidden. Their recoiling is not due to any defect in your call to them; rather, the defect lies in their faculties of perception. So trust in Allah in managing your affair concerning them;

Then he gave the reason for what the context has guided us to supply as its implied meaning, or he begins a new statement for one who asks in astonishment about their turning away from the clear truth, with His saying: ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear﴾. That is: you cannot create hearing for those who are like the dead in not benefiting from their faculties, which are in perfect soundness, and when they hear the verses they turn away from them.

Since likening them to the dead was discouraging, he said, giving hope: ﴿Nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾. That is: you cannot renew that for them. He thus likened them, in respect of the obstinacy and bad disposition with which they were created, to the deaf.

Since they had added to that aversion and repulsion, becoming like the deaf one who turns away, and since the deaf person, when he faces forward, may perhaps benefit through his sight and understanding, he said: ﴿when they turn their backs and flee﴾. He thus gave them hope regarding the bringing about of hearing, should a state from God arise in them by which their hearts accept it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 27, verse 81:

When He likened them to the deaf, in that they hear only when they are facing (the speaker), He likened them to the blind, in that they are not guided at all in any direction without a shepherd whom neither lapse nor weariness distracts from them. So He said: ﴿And you cannot guide the blind away from their error﴾, i.e., you cannot bring about guidance permanently in the hearts of ﴿the blind﴾ [i.e., in their sight and their insight, removing them, moving them, and distancing them] ﴿away from their error﴾, from the path, in such a way that you preserve them from ever being diverted from it at all. For this none is capable except the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-Hayy al-Qayyum). The context, as you see, indicates that their disbelief is ranked in three degrees: the highest, like the disbelief of Abu Jahl; the middle, like that of 'Utba ibn Rabi'a; and the lowest, like that of Abu Talib and some of the hypocrites. More elaboration on this will come in Surat al-Rum.

Since he may have been prevented from calling them, He gave him hope of their submission and turning back by saying: ﴿You will not make hear﴾, i.e., you will not cause to hear with the hearing of benefit in its perfect form, at all times, ﴿except those who believe﴾, i.e., those whom We know to believe ﴿in Our signs﴾, by having made in them the capacity for hearing. Then He stated as a consequence of this, as evidence of their faith: ﴿so they are submitting (muslimun)﴾, i.e., in the utmost obedience to you in ease and hardship, having no choice and no will in any of the matters.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 27, verse 82:

When he had finished with the great warning to them, consoling him (ﷺ) regarding their affair, and concluded with the mention of Islam, he followed it with the mention of what they were promised, of what they had been hastening (for) in mockery of him (p-215), and he began with the beast which distinguishes the believer from others. So he said, confirming with the particle of confirmation: ﴿And when the word falls upon them﴾, i.e., when the time arrives at the occurrence of the threat, which is the meaning of "the word," and as if, because of its magnitude, there is no other word (for it) ﴿upon them﴾, some of it by actual coming and some of it by being very near. ﴿We will bring forth﴾ [i.e.,] by what We have of greatness ﴿for them﴾ from the portents of the Hour ﴿a beast﴾, and what a beast, in its terror and its greatness, in form and in character ﴿from the earth﴾, i.e., the earth of Makkah, which is the mother of the earth, because nothing remains after the sending of the most perfect of creation with the highest of the Books except the removal of the veil.

Since the expression "beast" might convey that it is like dumb animals that have no speech, He said: ﴿will speak to them﴾, i.e., with speech they understand. Al-Baghawi narrated through the route of Muslim from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The first of the signs to emerge will be the rising of the sun from its west, and the emergence of the beast upon the people in the forenoon, and whichever of the two occurs before its companion, the other will follow it closely." And through the route of Ibn Khuzaymah from Abu Shurayhah al-Ghifari (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The beast will have three emergences in the course of time. It will emerge in the far reaches of Yemen, and its mention will spread among the desert dwellers, and its mention will not enter the town—meaning Makkah. Then it will remain for a long time. Then it will emerge in another emergence [near] Makkah, and its mention will spread among the desert dwellers and its mention will enter the town. Then while the people are one day in the greatest of the mosques in the sight of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in sanctity, and the most honoured of them in the sight of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic—meaning the Sacred Mosque—they will not be startled except by it in a corner of the mosque, drawing near and drawing near—thus said ʿAmr, meaning Ibn Muhammad al-ʿAbqari, one of the narrators of the hadith—between the Black Corner and the Gate of Banu Makhzum, on the right of one leaving, in the middle of that. The people will scatter away from it, but a band will stand firm, knowing that they will not frustrate Allah. Then it will come out upon them shaking the dust from its head, and it will pass by them and polish their faces until it leaves them like shining stars. Then it will turn away in the earth, none able to overtake it, and none able to escape it, until a man will stand and seek refuge from it in prayer, and it will come upon him from behind and say: 'O so-and-so! Now you are praying!' He will turn toward it with his face, and it will mark him on his face. People will then be neighbours in their homes, and will travel together, and will share their wealth; the disbeliever will be recognised from the believer, and it will be said to the believer: 'O believer!' and to the disbeliever: 'O disbeliever!'" And through the route of Imam Ahmad from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The beast will emerge with the staff of Musa and the seal of Sulayman (peace be upon them both). It will polish the face of the believer with the staff, and mark the nose of the disbeliever with the seal, until the people of the table (p-217) gather, and this one says: 'O believer!' and that one says: 'O disbeliever!'"

Then He, glory be to Him, gave the reason for bringing it forth with His words: ﴿that the people﴾, i.e., because they are people who have not reached the first age of faith, which is the age of those who believed; rather they are wavering, hesitating, vacillating at times and at other times ﴿were﴾, i.e., [in a state] which is for them like a natural disposition, ﴿in Our signs﴾, i.e., the visible things which We wrote by Our greatness in the essences of the world, and the audible recited things, which We brought to them upon the tongues of the most perfect of creation, the prophets and messengers, until We sealed them with their imam, who is the most perfect of the worlds, cutting off their argument and turning back their obstinacy; and for this reason We made his message general and made it obligatory upon all the rational to follow him, ﴿they are not certain﴾, from certainty, which is the perfection of knowledge with the negation of doubts; rather they are in them unsettled. So nothing remains after him (ﷺ) except the removal of the veil from that which is not of the kind of mankind, by that which their intellects cannot sustain.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 27, verse 83:

Since it is the act of the beast to distinguish between the believer and the disbeliever by that which they cannot repel, he followed it with the distinguishing of each of the two groups from its companion, gathering them on the Day of Resurrection into one place and driving them without mixing with the other group. So he said, conjoining it to the governing element in "وإذا وقَعَ القَوْلُ" (and when the Word falls upon them): ﴿And on the Day We gather﴾, i.e., We gather, by Our greatness, by way of compulsion. Abu Hayyan said: al-Hashr (the gathering) is the assembling (p-218) with violence. ﴿from every nation a crowd﴾, i.e., a large company. ﴿of those who deny﴾, i.e., [who cause denial to the guides] continuously, [scorning] ﴿Our signs﴾, i.e., the visible ones, by not taking heed of them, and the audible ones, by rejecting them and disparaging them, despite their greatness through their being attributed to Us. He indicated their great number by his saying [as a consequence of the governing element of the adverbial phrase, such as: they will be in great humiliation]: ﴿so they will be driven on﴾, i.e., they are restrained with the least gesture [from Him], the first of them upon the last of them, and their outer ranks upon their middle ranks, so that they catch up with one another, and none of them strays, and they continue thus.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 27, verse 84:

﴿Until, when they came﴾, i.e., to the place which Allah had willed for their rebuke. ﴿He said﴾ to them, the King of kings, without manifesting to them a definitive judgment regarding what He knows of their state in their obstinacy and their misguidance; rather, He asked them, to make justice manifest by obligating them with what they themselves acknowledge. In this there is denunciation, reproach, rebuke, and censure: ﴿"Did you deny My signs"﴾, i.e., [O] you ignorant ones, ﴿despite their greatness in themselves, and their coming to you upon the hands of the noblest of My servants"﴾, ﴿"while you had not encompassed them in knowledge"﴾, i.e., without reflection or consideration that would lead to encompassing their meanings and that for which they were manifested, so that you would know what they deserve and what befits them, by an indubitable proof. ﴿"Or what was it that you were doing"﴾, i.e., in those times, with what is for you like innate dispositions, ﴿"[in] their [regard]?"﴾: did you believe in them, or did you deny them after encompassing their knowledge? Inform Me about all of that! What ailed you, that you did not occupy yourselves with this important task? For this - by My might - is a station of justice and verification, in which not even a speck (qitmir) nor a date-pit (naqir) is left aside, and no injustice is done to anyone, in what is great or small, little or much. And the question in this manner alerts to the compulsion to either affirm or acknowledge the falsehood, for if they say, "We denied," then if they say so without having encompassed it, it is in the utmost clarity of falsehood; and if they say so while having encompassed it, it is the most lying of lies.

Since the implied sense, as the context indicates, is: "So they answered with what showed that they were wrongdoers," he connected to it His saying: ﴿And the word shall fall﴾, i.e., the content of the threat, which is the word, becoming true, established ﴿upon them because of what they wronged﴾, i.e., because of the wrongdoing that proceeded from them, namely plain denial and the misguidance that arose from it, in their sayings and their deeds; ﴿so they will not speak﴾, i.e., because of what occupied them of the descent of the punishment threatened against them, which encompassed their powers, shattered their foundations, and because of what became clear to them, that nothing would save them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 27, verse 86:

When he mentioned the gathering (al-hashr, the assembling of people for judgment), he argued for it by their being gathered each night to their beds, by the sealing of their senses, by their being roused from sleep, and by the manifestation of darkness, which is like death after light, and the raising of light after its extinction by darkness. So he said: ﴿Do they not see﴾ what indicates to them Our power to resurrect them after death and to [bring about] all that We have informed them of, ﴿that We made﴾, i.e., by Our greatness, to which no one can attain resemblance in any respect (p-220) [which indicates Our singularity and that We act by choice], ﴿the night﴾, i.e., dark, ﴿so that they may rest therein﴾ from dispersing, ﴿and the day as giving sight﴾, i.e., giving sight to whoever is in it, so that they may disperse therein for their livelihoods after they had died the lesser death. How many a person among them has spent the night sound, with no ailment, and then died! Had We willed, We would have made all of them so, and none of them would have risen. He turned away from "that they may see therein" to draw attention to the perfection of its being a cause of seeing, and to the fact that the purpose is not like the resting; rather, rest is a means to the intended purpose, which is the attainment of benefits. So the verse is of the type of al-ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which two complementary elements are mentioned and each one's omitted counterpart is implied by the other): mentioning rest first indicates dispersal [second], and mentioning seeing second indicates darkness first. Then he magnified this verse, urging reflection on the guiding power in it that leads to the right path, and so he said: ﴿Indeed in that﴾, i.e., in the gathering and the lesser raising together with the two signs of night and day, ﴿are signs﴾, i.e., numerous and clear indications of tawhid (the oneness of God), of the other resurrection, and of prophethood (nubuwwah), because whoever alternates the two alternating [phenomena] for the benefit of people in this world sends messengers for their benefit in the two abodes.

(p-221) Since it is among the foundations of the surah to restrict guidance to the believers, He specified the signs for them because they alone benefit from them, although all are shared in their being an indication for them. So He said: ﴿for a people who believe﴾, i.e., I have decreed that their faith continually renews itself, so they are each day in ascent and elevation.

When he mentioned this particular gathering, and the proof for the general resurrection and raising, he mentioned the general gathering, lest it be thought that He gathers only the disbelievers. So he said, indicating their generality in death just as He encompassed them in sleep, and their generality in revival just as He encompassed them in waking: ﴿And the day the Horn is blown﴾, that is, with the easiest of matters, ﴿into the Horn﴾, that is, the trumpet (al-qarn) whose sound was made to cause the death of all.

Since what arises from their terror, together with its being certain and definitively decided, is as though it has already occurred and passed, and will happen in a single instant, he indicated this and the swiftness of its occurrence by using the past tense, saying: ﴿and terror seizes﴾, that is, swoons because of this blowing, ﴿whoever is in the heavens﴾.

Since the matter is terrifying, elaboration (al-iṭnāb, expansive wording) is more fitting, so he said: ﴿and whoever is on the earth﴾, that is, all of them, ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾, that is, He who encompasses all in knowledge, power, might and majesty, that they should not be terrified. Then he pointed to the blowing for the revival of all by His saying: ﴿and all﴾, that is, whoever was terrified and whoever was not, ﴿will come to Him﴾, that is, (p-222) after that, for the reckoning, by another blowing through which He will raise them up, as a proof of the complete power in His bringing them back by that by which He made them sleep, ﴿humbled﴾, that is, abased and broken.

He dispensed with stating this explicitly, because it is known by self-evident reasoning (al-badīha) that they cannot come while in the state of their terror, which is a kināya (allusion, metonymy) for the loss of their senses. This is the meaning of what many of the exegetes have said. What fits the context of the preceding verses, since the discourse concerns the Day of Resurrection, which is the time-frame for what lies between the resurrection and the entry of the two groups into their two abodes, is that this blowing occurs after the resurrection, and that by a mere swoon, which is like fainting, just as the gathering of the groups is likewise. This is supported by the expression "terror," and the coming after it will be by another blowing through which the standing up occurs. These two blowings, then, are what is meant by his saying (ﷺ): "People will swoon on the Day of Resurrection," the hadith, and its wording and meaning will be discussed later, Allah willing, and what it contains of difficulty will be addressed at the end of Surat az-Zumar.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 27, verse 88:

When He mentioned their humiliation (dukhur), He followed it with the humiliation of something far greater in creation and more awesome in matter, so He said: [conjoining with the verb governing the adverbial phrase, the implied sense being: "there will be matters loosened"], expressing it in the present tense (al-mudari'), because that, although it shares with the terror (al-faza') in being realized, differs from it in occurring and renewing itself gradually, bit by bit: ﴿And you see the mountains﴾, meaning: at the time of rising from the graves. The address is either to the Prophet (ﷺ), so that this indicates the magnitude of the matter, since he (ﷺ) was the most piercing of people in sight and the brightest in insight, or it is to everyone, because all of them, after rising, become fit to be addressed, after having been hidden in the dust. ﴿You think them solid﴾, meaning: standing firm and fixed in their place, not moving, because every great thing whose extremities are far apart has its motion not perceived except by conjecture. ﴿And they pass by﴾, meaning: they move along until they become like carded wool (al-'ihn al-manfush), and then Allah blows them away so that they fall wherever He wills, like scattered dust (al-habaʾ al-mansur), so that the whole earth becomes level, with no crookedness in it. He indicated that their movement is hidden, although it is swift, by His saying: ﴿The passing of clouds﴾, meaning: a swift passing that is not perceived as it truly is, because when it covers the sky its movement is not perceived, though there is no doubt about it, even when the sun is not uncovered, without ambiguity. Likewise, every object of great bulk or great number is beyond being encompassed by the sight, because of the distance between its extremities due to its abundance; it is moving, while the sharp observer thinks it stationary.

Since that was a stupendous matter, He pointed to its greatness by His saying, emphasizing the content of the preceding sentence: ﴿The handiwork of Allah﴾, meaning: the handiwork of Him to whom all affairs belong, that which He informed us will occur on that day as a handiwork. Such a verbal noun (masdar), when it comes after a statement, serves as a witness to its truth, a herald of its rightness, and a proclamation of its exalted worth, and that it could not have been other than this. Then He increased the magnification by His saying, indicating the completeness of perfection in that handiwork: ﴿who perfected everything﴾.

Since this was established in this perfectly crafted manner and most firmly ordered system, it produced with certainty His saying: ﴿Indeed He is Aware of what you do﴾, meaning: the One who perfected all these matters is ﴿Aware of what you do﴾. This is because perfection is the result of power, and power is the result of knowledge; whoever is not all-encompassing in knowledge is not perfect in power. He expressed it with the verb (fi'l), which is more general than being with knowledge or not, because it is in the context of clarifying their blindness and the negation of knowledge from them. It was also read with the second-person address (al-khitab), which signals nearness that is hoped to lead to approval, and warns against distance that is coupled with wrath, and with the third-person (al-ghayba), which signals turning away that brings about disappointment. How wonderfully this fits and is joined with what follows it, as an answer, implicitly, to a question as if someone asked: "What will be the state of the people of the gathering along with the humiliation, in the view of the discerning critic?" Then He answered: from His perfecting of things is that He arranged the recompense in the most excellent arrangement.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 27, verse 89:

﴿Whoever brings a good deed﴾, i.e., the complete one, which is faith; ﴿for him﴾, and this is part of His perfect arrangement of things, ﴿there is better﴾, i.e., more excellent, ﴿than it﴾, multiplied: the least of it is ten times over, up to what none knows but Allah, [and their faces shall be spared from the Fire], and these are the people of nearness (p-225) ﴿for whom the best reward has preceded﴾. ﴿And they will be safe from the terror of that Day﴾, i.e., when these great and terrifying states occur, ﴿secure﴾, i.e., so that the greatest terror will not grieve them. Consider the eloquence of this speech, the excellence of its arrangement and ordering, and how each part takes hold of the next, as if they were all frightened by a single fright. For a matter such as this has rendered the strong helpless and silenced the boasting and the vain claims.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 27, verse 90:

﴿Whoever comes with an evil deed﴾ — i.e., one for which there is no evil like it, which is shirk (associating partners with God), as His saying indicates: ﴿their faces will be thrown into the Fire﴾ — i.e., with the easiest of matters ﴿into the Fire﴾, even though it has been reported in the Sahih (authentic collection) that "the places of prostration, the noblest of which are the faces, are not a path for the Fire upon them." The face is the noblest thing in a human being, so when it is humiliated, what is other than it is more deserving of humiliation. And "the one thrown upon his face" is one who is turned upside down.

Since they had turned their deeds upside down and reversed them by worshipping other than God, they placed things in other than their proper places: they magnified what deserved to be belittled, and treated lightly the command of the Most High, the Great. The face is the locus of the manifestation of modesty and humility, given the manifestation of the proof; yet they had stared with their eyes in boldness and harshness when obstinate, and displayed in their faces scowling, frowning and turning away. By way of a reversal, His saying [based on what is implied by the ihtibak (interlocking of meanings), namely: ﴿and they will be secure from terror that Day﴾ is understood as: "and they, from the terror of that Day, will be fearful, and for them there is nothing but the like of their evil deed"]: ﴿Are you being recompensed?﴾ — i.e., being told: "Are you being recompensed" — ﴿except for what you used to do﴾ — i.e., with what is natural to you, as if it were innate — ﴿work﴾ — i.e., you repeat its work, while you claim that it is founded upon the rules of knowledge, [such that] everyone who sees it testifies that it is identical to your deeds, exactly alike. It also encompasses the people of the first category as well. [The verse is an example of ihtibak: it mentions "better" and "security" first, as an indication of the omission of "its like" and "fear" second; and it mentions "thrown into the Fire" second, as an indication of "honour" being omitted first.]

When he had completed the religion by mentioning its three foundations, the origin (al-mabda'), the return (al-ma'ad), and prophethood (al-nubuwwah), together with the preliminaries of the Resurrection and its conditions, [and some of its attributes and what will occur of its terrors], and this is the completion of what pertains to the foundations of the religion in ways that encourage with the most complete encouragement and warn with the greatest warning, this encouragement and warning necessarily obliged every hearer to say: "So what should we do [and whom should we worship]?" The one addressed by this revelation answered them, the one commanded to convey these comprehensive matters, who calls those who hear him and guides those who follow him, that he does not desire for them what he desires for himself, and this is what his Lord commanded him. So He said: ﴿Indeed, I have only been commanded﴾ [i.e., by the command of One whose command cannot be reversed]. It is not far-fetched that this is a substitute for His saying: ﴿Praise be to God, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen﴾ [al-Naml: 59], so that its position is in the accusative by the verb "say." (p-227) [And He magnified what he was commanded with by placing it in the position of the principal element, and said]: ﴿to worship﴾, i.e., with all that He has commanded you, ﴿the Lord﴾, i.e., the Bringer-into-being, the Manager, and the King. He specified the intended one and singled him out [and brought him near] as an honour and a mark of dignity by saying: ﴿of this city﴾, i.e., Makkah, the one from which the beast will emerge, so that everyone who sees it will be terrified, and then it will grant security to the people of happiness. I single it out with this; I do not worship anything of what you have equated with Him, may He be glorified, and claimed to be partners, while they are themselves part of what He created. Then He described the object of worship, the One whom He has not commanded worship of anyone other than Him, with what the attribute of lordship (al-rububiyyah) requires, and with the determination of the city to which He pointed with the demonstrative of proximity, because it is present in minds on account of its greatness and the strong familiarity with it, and because it is intended by "the land from which the beast emerges." Thus it became such that when "the city" is mentioned without qualification, the mind turns to it and it is recognised as Makkah. So He said: ﴿who has made it sacred﴾, reminding them of His blessing upon them and His nurturing of them, by settling them in the best of His lands, and by making them thereby an object of awe in the hearts of His servants, through what He placed in hearts of its being a sanctuary [in which no blood is shed], nobody is wronged, game is not hunted, and its trees are not cut, and He singled it out from among all His other lands, while people are snatched away from around them, whereas they are secure, and nothing of their terror and dread reaches them. (p-228) Since its attribution to Him is only for the sake of pure honour, He said, as a precaution against what might be suspected: ﴿and to Him belongs everything﴾, i.e., of other than it, of what you have associated with Him and others, in creation, dominion, and possession, and He is not like kings, who possess only what they protect against others.

Since they might say: "We also worship Him by worshipping those whom we hope will bring us near to Him in nearness," He specified the religion by which worship is performed, and said: ﴿And I have been commanded﴾, i.e., together with the command to worship Him alone, [and He magnified the object commanded by making it the principal of the speech, by placing it in the position of the agent, and said]: ﴿to be﴾, i.e., in a state that is at the utmost firmness, ﴿among the Muslims﴾, i.e., those who submit to everything His Book commands with the most complete submission, steadfast in that to the utmost steadfastness.

When he had explained what he was commanded regarding himself, he followed it with what its benefit extends to others, saying: ﴿And that I should recite the Qur'an﴾, meaning: I should persist in its recitation (tilawa) and its following (talw), that is, following it, as worship to my Lord, and as conveying to the people what I have been sent with to them, which is of such a nature that doubt does not touch it, that it is from Him, [and that I may be] one who keeps His commands in mind, so that I act upon them, and His prohibitions, so that I avoid them, and so that the people may turn to him and rely upon him in every matter, because he comprises every knowledge.

When, as a consequence of this, whoever submits to him saves his own soul, and whoever rebels against him destroys it, his Lord, glorified is He, said to him, consoling him, comforting him, encouraging him, and warning him: ﴿So whoever is guided﴾, meaning: by following this Qur'an, which calls to the Gardens, ﴿then he is guided only for his own self﴾, because it gives life to his soul by securing reward and his deliverance from punishment, [so I am only one of the bringers of good news, bringing him the good news that he is among those who are saved]. ﴿And whoever goes astray﴾, meaning: away from the path that He laid down and made clear, without inclination or crookedness, ﴿then say﴾ to him, as you say to others: ﴿I am only one of the warners﴾, meaning: one who frightens him with the consequences of his deeds. He explained and repeated this, since I have not yet been commanded to do anything about him now. (p. 229)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 27, verse 93:

﴿Say﴾ — that is, as a warning to them, and as encouragement, hope, and intimidation: ﴿Praise﴾ — that is, the complete ascription of all attributes of perfection ﴿belongs to Allah﴾ — that is, the One to whom all greatness belongs, whether all of them are guided and all of them go astray, or they divide into those who are guided and those who are astray, because nothing escapes His will.

Since the result of this is power over everything, He said: ﴿He will show you His signs﴾ — that is, in this world and the Hereafter, by a promise that is certain, with no doubt about its occurrence — ﴿so you will recognize them﴾. That is, His signs which turn you back from what you are engaged in, on the day when this city, which He has made sacred, is made lawful for me, by what is indicated by my being made one of the warners, and other than that, what appears of its events and becomes известный of its days, which the Qur'an stated explicitly or hinted at, so that its interpretation comes to you and you see it with your own eyes. This is the meaning of ﴿so you will recognize them﴾, that is, by your recalling what I now threaten you with and describe to you (p-230) of them, you will have no doubt or suspicion regarding any of that, that it is as I have described it. Thus the greatness of the Qur'an will become manifest to you, and the clarity of the signs of the Book, which is the Criterion, and you will see that with the certainty of truth. ﴿And you will surely know its news after a while﴾ [Sad: 88] ﴿On the day its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say: "The messengers of our Lord have certainly come with the truth"﴾ [al-A'raf: 53] ﴿"This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 52].

Since He had given them respite with the particle "sin" regarding their terms, and the implied meaning was as consolation to him ﷺ: "Your Lord will not leave them in this state of obstinacy, because your Lord is able to do what He wills," He joined to it His saying: ﴿And your Lord is not unaware﴾ — that is, the One who has been good to you by all that He has established you in of these great matters and magnificent conditions — ﴿of what you do﴾ — that is, of opposing His commands and departing from His prohibitions. It is permissible that the clause be a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the subject of "yurā" (He shows), meaning: He shows you while not being unaware. And whoever recited with the second person (taʿmalūn) the meaning would be: of what you and your followers do of obedience, and of disobedience, so He will recompense each of you according to what he deserves, [He will exalt your affair, strengthen your support, weaken their resolve, and diminish their scheming, by what He possesses of wisdom, knowledge, and the executing of His word. So let no one suppose that His leaving the dealing with them by punishment is out of heedlessness of any of their deeds; rather, that is because He has set for them a limit which they will surely reach, since His word is not changed in His presence. Thus its last part has returned, as you see, to the clarity of the Book, the magnification of the Qur'an, and the division of people within it into the guided and the astray, back to its beginning, and its conclusion has embraced its opening with the wisdom of its Sender and the knowledge of its whole and its details,] and other matters that become apparent upon its reflection and contemplation. And Allah is the Granter of success to what is correct, and to Him is the return and the final place.

The blessed part of al-Biqa'i's Munasabat is completed, by the praise and help of Allah, and it is followed by al-Qasas, God willing. O Allah, forgive us our sins and pass over our misdeeds.
